hypothesis: A 512-particle shared-memory tile may reduce synchronization rounds relative to the previously measured 256-particle tile while preserving the pairwise arithmetic and source order. Its larger shared-memory footprint may offset that benefit; the controller's correctness suite and timing protocol must decide.
notes: Changed only the kernel. With the supplied 256-thread launch, each thread loads up to two source particles per 512-entry tile. Both barriers are block-uniform, including for partial target blocks and the final partial source tile. The new candidate has not been measured; launch configuration and shared-memory limits were not changed.
transformations: Replace the 256-entry static shared-memory source tile with a 512-entry tile while leaving the 256-thread launch settings unchanged.
Load tile entries cooperatively with a thread-strided loop and keep both block barriers unconditional so partial tiles and inactive target threads synchronize uniformly.
Preserve the source iteration order, pairwise force expression, self-interaction skip, and copied output mass.
